newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus on Daimler as German bourse opens mixed.
newsitem.headline: Focus on Daimler as German bourse opens mixed.

text.p: German equities were mixed as bourse trade opened on Thursday, with the market awaiting first-half earnings news from German industrial conglomerate Daimler-Benz to give it some kind of direction.
The DAX index, which measures trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, was down 3.58 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,559.58.

The backdrop to early bourse trade was not particularly encouraging, with the dollar still weak and with the close on Wall Street overnight having a neutral effect. However, firmer German bonds underpinned trade early on.
"We're looking at a range of between 2,550 and 2,570 points over the day, with the market tending downwards," said one Frankfurt trader.
Daimler Benz shares were up 38 pfennigs at 81.70 marks in early bourse trade.
Analysts told Reuters on Wednesday that they expected Daimler's half-year results to show the conglomerate had rebounded from 1995, when Daimler posted the highest loss ever seen at a German company.
German carmaker Volkswagen AG was higher in early bourse trade, boosted by news that its subsidiary Audi AG first-half pretax profits were up 58 percent at 405 million marks.
This combined with Wednesday's news that VW's west European delivery figures were higher to lift the share 1.50 marks to 553 marks.

Shares in electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG were lower after reports that Iran was suing the company for 5.4 billion dollars for failing to complete an Iranian nuclear power plant abandoned after the 1979 Islamic revolution.
In early bourse trade Siemens were down 1.18 marks at 78.10 marks.
